source: External review of the RL setup (algorithm, action space, discount, critic, dataset, reward).

action_space_900d.claim: 900-D action space is shockingly high for SAC given the data size; the critic cannot estimate value and the actor exploits critic error.
action_space_900d.verified: CONFIRMED AND QUANTIFIED. Action = 30 dims x 30 horizon = 900, fed to the critic as a flat vector (MultiQHead(HID, 30*H, ...)). Available data at the analysed checkpoint: ~6919 online chunks + 467 demo chunks = ~7386 transitions -> 8.2 samples per action dimension. SAC's actor objective is to maximise the critic, so it climbs exactly the interpolation error of a critic fitted that sparsely.
action_space_900d.fix: g1_piston_action_basis.py: fixed orthonormal DCT-II projection of each joint's 30-step trajectory onto 6 smooth components. Critic action input 900 -> 180 (8.2 -> 41 samples per dim). Measured on 245 real demonstration chunks: 99.9994% retained energy, RMSE 0.002 rad. Linear, fixed, no parameters, applied ONLY to the critic's view -- the actor still emits and the robot still executes the full chunk, so the policy class and deployment are unchanged.

dimensions_not_independent.claim: Action dimensions are not independent; they depend on hand/arm configuration and time. PPO / Diffusion RL may be needed.
dimensions_not_independent.verified: CORRECT and only PARTLY addressed. The policy is a diagonal-covariance squashed Gaussian over 900 scalars, which is a factorised distribution: it cannot represent correlations between joints or across time within a chunk. The DCT basis fixes the CRITIC's view (low-order coefficients ARE the temporal structure) but does not change the policy class.
dimensions_not_independent.honest_limitation: A factorised Gaussian over action chunks remains the actor. Making the policy itself structured is a policy-class change -- PPO with a structured/autoregressive head, or a diffusion/flow-matching policy (e.g. Chi et al., Diffusion Policy, RSS 2023; Ren et al., DPPO, 2024) -- which is a re-architecture, not a parameter change, and is NOT claimed to be done here.
dimensions_not_independent.status: PARTIAL: critic-side fixed; actor-side recorded as an open architectural item.

measured.data: 245 real demonstration action chunks (30 steps x 30 dims = 900 scalars each).
measured.interpretation: The reviewer's point is quantitatively severe. Real action chunks live on a ~16-dimensional manifold inside a 900-dimensional space: 2 components explain 90% of variance and 16 explain 99.9%. A diagonal-covariance Gaussian over 900 scalars models that space as 900 independent axes, so almost all of its probability mass sits on trajectories the robot never produces. Temporal coupling dominates (same joint across time, mean |corr| 0.644) over cross-joint coupling at a fixed time (0.222), which is exactly the structure the DCT basis captures -- and is why the critic-side fix is well matched to the data even though the actor remains factorised.
measured.why_this_supports_the_recommended_direct: With an intrinsic dimensionality near 16, a policy class that models the joint distribution -- PPO with a structured head, or a diffusion/flow policy -- is not a stylistic preference but a match to the measured data geometry. Untested here; stated as the recommended next architecture, not as a result.

discount_too_small.claim: gamma too small: 0.99^30 = 0.74 per chunk, and 0.74^20 = 0.25 of terminal reward seen at the start.
discount_too_small.verified: CONFIRMED, and worse than stated for the actual episode length. GAMMA was literally 0.99 ** H with H=30 -> 0.7397 per chunk. Episodes are EP_CHUNKS=23, so terminal credit at episode start was 0.7397^23 = 0.0010 -- one tenth of one percent, i.e. numerically invisible. On a task whose payoff is entirely terminal this alone prevents the behaviour from being learned.
discount_too_small.fix: The discount is now specified directly at the chunk level, where the decision happens: GAMMA_CHUNK, default 0.98 -> 0.98^23 = 0.63 of terminal reward visible at episode start (equivalent per-step gamma 0.99933). The run config records gamma_chunk, terminal_credit_at_episode_start and equivalent_per_step_gamma.

critic_needs_state_and_phase.claim: Critic should have access to proprioceptive state and phase label; pure RGB is too weak.
critic_needs_state_and_phase.verified: CONFIRMED: the critic saw only the frozen VLM's pooled feature of a single 424x240 RGB frame. That cannot disambiguate joint configuration behind occlusion, a few millimetres of plunger travel inside the grip, or -- decisively -- WHICH STAGE the episode is in. Reward is stage-gated, so the same image carries different value depending on which stages already fired; inferring that from one frame is impossible in principle.
critic_needs_state_and_phase.fix: g1_piston_critic_state.py: privileged vector of right arm+hand joint positions and velocities, fingertip/thumb offsets in the barrel frame, barrel and rod pose and velocity, plunger position and velocity, barrel relative to tube and pot, an 8-way phase one-hot, and normalized episode progress. Standard asymmetric actor-critic (Pinto et al. 2017): the actor still sees only RGB, so deployment is unchanged; the critic is discarded at deployment so privilege is free.

dataset_does_not_succeed.verified: CONFIRMED, on two independent axes already measured in this study. (1) Under the embodiment, only 22 of 67 dataset episodes are executable at all (g1_piston_demo_screen_manifest.json) -- the dataset labels all 67 as success. (2) Under the FUNCTIONAL predicate, only 3 of 11 replayed demonstrations depress the plunger past half travel; the rest show only passive gripping compliance (g1_piston_plunger_dof.json). So the demonstrations are weak supervision for the task as named, which is consistent with SFT scoring 0.00 deterministic success.
dataset_does_not_succeed.consequence: RLPD's offline half is a weak prior for the functional act, and the press must largely be discovered from reward. Recorded rather than papered over.

reward_unreasonable.claim: Reward setting is not reasonable (xy-only grasp, throwable lift, sky success, no smoothness, stale validation).
reward_unreasonable.verified: CONFIRMED on every sub-point; see g1_piston_reward_v3_review_fixes.json for the per-point evidence, including a direct reproduction of the sky-throw success under both v1 and v2.

net_effect: Before: a 900-D critic input at 8 samples/dim, terminal credit 0.001, an RGB-only critic, and a reward that awarded success to a pipette floating 0.8 m in the air. After: 180-D critic input at 41 samples/dim, terminal credit 0.63, a critic with proprioception and phase, and a reward requiring a genuine 3-D opposed grasp, a plunger press, and a released at-rest placement inside a supported height band.
not_claimed: The actor remains a factorised Gaussian over chunks. Whether PPO or a diffusion policy would outperform this SAC/RLPD setup on this task is untested here and is stated as an open question, not a result.
